item.title: 'Rivers in the sky' influence marine heat waves
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Long, narrow bands of moving moisture in the sky, known as atmospheric rivers, contribute to heat waves in the marine environment, according to a new study published in Nature Communications by researchers from Duke University's Nicholas School of the Environment. The study is the first to analyze the association between these "rivers in the sky" and marine heat waves, paving the way for future research on the mechanisms at play and how climate change factors in.

item.title: Impact of climate change may be equivalent to 3.3 million years of transformations in tropical vegetation
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — The tropics cover less than one-third of Earth's surface but are home to more than half of all known species. Forests, savannas, grasslands and deserts: A vast array of environments stretches along the planet's equatorial belt. This diversity, however, is not static. It is the result of millions of years of changes that have reshaped the tropical landscape time and again.

item.title: Mesolithic hunter-gatherers on Malta relied on repeated sea crossings, study suggests
item.description: [Foraging & Wild Plants] Keyword: forager — The existence of humans on Malta, a tiny Mediterranean island, during the Mesolithic period is puzzling. Archaeological evidence indicates that foragers occupied the Maltese islands between 8,500 and 7,500 years ago, and it is hypothesized that they arrived by sea. How did they survive over such an extended period, given the limited resources available on this small island?

item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: type 2 diabetes — A healthy lifestyle can prevent type 2 diabetes for many people, but new research suggests that weight loss alone may not be enough for one particularly vulnerable group. item.title: Misfolded insulin may be quietly driving diabetes
